description: Let members save addresses on their profile (an address book) and require an address to be provided before a purchase or a trade proceeds. Today there is NO saved-address concept: profiles has no address columns; delivery addresses are entered per-contract in the cash-sale terms dialog / trade negotiation and stored on the contract (cash_sales delivery_* columns, trade_delivery_details). acceptCashSaleTerms already refuses a DELIVERY cash sale without an address, but there is no saved address to reuse and no required-address prompt surfaced early or for trades in a way the user considers sufficient. This feature adds a reusable saved-address book and makes address entry a required, prefilled step before committing to a purchase or trade. This is the largest, most architectural part - respect the domain privacy invariant: a contract's delivery address remains PRIVATE per-contract data; saved addresses are only a convenience SOURCE the member copies from, never auto-disclosed.
steps: Design the saved-address store. Add a new table cardtrade.member_addresses (or similar) via a new sequential migration file supabase/migrations/0113_member_addresses.sql following the conventions in 0085/0086: owner id (references profiles/auth user), a human label, the provider-resolved place fields already used elsewhere (address_label, place_id, country_code, latitude, longitude - mirror cash_sale_return_details / delivery columns), an optional is_default boolean, timestamps. Add RLS so a member can only select/insert/update/delete their OWN addresses. Do NOT expose addresses in public_profiles. Add a column comment explaining the table is a private convenience address book, distinct from per-contract delivery addresses.

Hand-update lib/supabase/database.types.ts to add the new table's Row/Insert/Update types, matching the surrounding hand-maintained style and comments. (There is no live DB in-sandbox to regenerate types; the file is maintained by hand.)

Add server actions for the address book in a new lib/actions/addresses.ts ('use server'), following the thin-authenticated-action pattern (authenticate via session, authorize against the caller's own id - never trust a passed-in owner id). Provide: listMyAddresses, saveAddress (create/update, validating the place is provider-resolved via the existing isResolvedPlace/isResolvedAddress helpers in domain/fulfilment/terms.ts), deleteAddress, and setDefaultAddress. Use the cookie-bound client so RLS scopes writes; validate label length and reject unresolved (text:/legacy:) places.

Add a profile settings UI to manage saved addresses. Locate the profile settings surface (lib/actions/profile.ts drives it; find the profile page/tab under app/ - e.g. profile 'profile' tab). Add an 'Addresses' section that lists saved addresses, lets the member add one using the existing components/location PlaceSearch/PlacePicker primitives (reuse PlaceMap for confirmation per the established pattern), edit label / set default, and delete. Match existing profile-section component structure (see how bio/social links sections are built).

Wire saved addresses into the BUY flow so an address is required before purchase and prefilled from the book. In the cash-sale DELIVERY path (components/sales/CashSaleTermsDialog.tsx + components/fulfilment/FulfilmentTermsFields.tsx, which already has showDeliveryAddress/deliveryAddress props), let the buyer pick a saved address (dropdown/list sourced from listMyAddresses) or enter a new one with an option to save it to the book. Keep the existing per-contract storage (the chosen address is copied onto the contract as it is today) and keep the existing acceptCashSaleTerms guard that refuses DELIVERY without a configured address. Ensure the requirement is clearly surfaced BEFORE the buyer commits, not only as a late error.

Wire saved addresses into the TRADE flow the same way for posted (DELIVERY) trades: the trade delivery-address entry (updateTradeHandoverTerms / the trade negotiation address field, gated by *_delivery_address_configured) should offer the saved-address book as a source and require an address before the posted trade can proceed to the state that needs it. Preserve the invariant that a trader may not read the OTHER trader's address until collateral locks. Use 'card hold'/'collateral' language, never 'escrow', for trades.

Handle the IN_PERSON case correctly: an in-person purchase/trade needs a meeting place (already required by validateFulfilmentTerms), NOT a postal address - do not force a saved postal address on in-person handovers. The 'address required before purchase/trade' requirement applies to the delivery/postal method (and to the meeting place for in-person, which is already enforced).

Add tests: server-action tests for addresses.ts (create/list/update/delete/default, rejecting unresolved places and enforcing owner-scoping) following the lib/actions test patterns; and tests covering that the buy/trade delivery flows require an address and can source it from the book. Reuse existing fakes/helpers (tests/e2e/support/payments.ts shows the saved-card precondition pattern; unit tests use fakes in tests/unit/fakes). Keep domain validation tests (tests/property/fulfilmentTerms.test.ts) green.
acceptance_criteria: A signed-in member can save, edit, set-default, and delete postal addresses from their profile settings, and these persist (new member_addresses table + RLS scoping to the owner).
Saved addresses are NEVER exposed via public_profiles or to other members except through the existing per-contract disclosure rules.

Starting a DELIVERY purchase requires a delivery address and the buyer can select one from their saved address book (or enter+save a new one); the requirement is surfaced before commitment, and the existing acceptCashSaleTerms guard still blocks paying a DELIVERY sale with no address.

A posted (DELIVERY) trade requires an address before it can proceed to the state that needs it, sourcing from the saved book, without breaking the invariant that the counterparty's address is hidden until collateral locks.
In-person purchases/trades are unaffected (meeting place still required, no postal address forced).
New migration follows conventions; database.types.ts updated by hand to match; server actions authorize against session identity only.
New tests cover the address book actions and the required-address gating; typecheck, lint (no new errors), and the existing suite (minus the 8 pre-existing Flutter failures) stay green.
verification: npm test (new address tests pass; no regression to previously-passing tests; the 8 Flutter-agreement failures remain the only failures)
Review the migration SQL and RLS for owner-scoping correctness and confirm public_profiles was not widened to include addresses
findings: Implemented in full. New migration supabase/migrations/0113_member_addresses.sql creates cardtrade.member_addresses (owner_id, optional label, provider-resolved place fields mirroring cash_sale_delivery_details, is_default with a partial unique index for one-default-per-owner, RLS scoping every op to auth.uid()=owner_id). public_profiles was NOT widened. database.types.ts hand-updated with the Row/Insert/Update block + Relationship. New server actions lib/actions/addresses.ts (listMyAddresses/saveAddress/deleteAddress/setDefaultAddress): authorize against session id only, filter every write by owner_id (belt-and-braces on RLS), validate provider-resolved place via domain isResolvedPlace, reject text:/legacy: and over-length labels. Profile 'Addresses' section: components/profile/MemberAddressesEditor.tsx + AddressesSettingRow wired into app/(workspace)/profile/page.tsx (count read with head:true). Buy flow: new components/fulfilment/SavedAddressField.tsx (pick saved / enter+optionally-save), rendered by FulfilmentTermsFields via new deliveryAddressFromBook/prefillDefaultAddress props, enabled in CashSaleTermsDialog for the buyer; existing acceptCashSaleTerms guard and per-contract copy-onto-contract behaviour unchanged. Trade flow: DeliveryAddressPanel edit dialog now sources from the book via SavedAddressField, editing ONLY the viewer's own address (counterparty stays RLS-gated until collateral locks; existing *_delivery_address_configured gating untouched). IN_PERSON path unchanged (meeting place still required by validateFulfilmentTerms; no postal address forced). Tests: tests/unit/addressesAction.test.ts (16: create/list/update/delete/default, unresolved-place + over-length rejection, owner-scoping, demote-before-promote) and tests/component/savedAddressField.test.tsx (5: chooser render, default prefill, no-overwrite, selection reports source, empty book). Verification: npm run typecheck clean; npm run lint shows only the pre-existing scripts/lib/mobileContract.ts error + 3 pre-existing warnings (no new); npm test 895 passing (874 baseline + 21 new), only the 8 pre-existing Flutter-agreement failures remain (mobileDomainAgreement 3 + mobileThemeAgreement 5); the ~11 jsdom matchMedia 'errors' in addPaymentMethodDialog/tradeFeeDisclosure are pre-existing teardown noise and those files' tests pass. NOTE: did not stage the uncommitted FEAT-002 files (lib/actions/cashSale.ts, tradeNegotiation.ts, trades.ts, lib/trades/collateralPlacement.ts, lib/webhook/webhookPipeline.ts, lib/notifications/settlementNotifier.ts + 3 settlement tests) — left them for their own feature.
